string.description: The universal representation. Every value is a string; the interpreter caches a typed internal form for speed.

list.description: A string with a canonical quoting convention. `llength`/`lindex` parse it and cache the parsed form.

dict.description: Ordered key/value mapping with value (copy-on-write) semantics, 8.5+.

integer.description: Arbitrary precision since 8.5; `expr` promotes as needed.

double.description: IEEE-754 double, used when an expression involves a decimal.

channel.description: Handle for a file, socket, pipe or serial port, from `open` or `socket`.

namespace.description: A container for commands and variables, qualified with `::`.

array.description: A collection of variables indexed by string, written `a(key)`. Not a value — it cannot be passed directly; use a dict for that.

bytearray.description: Internal binary representation, produced by `binary format` and `encoding convertto`.

command.description: A named procedure. Commands are first-class by name, and `rename` can redefine them.

coroutine.description: A resumable call frame, created by `coroutine` and suspended by `yield`.
